recipes.name: Linda's Cranberry Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.5 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease two baking sheets.

Combine flour and baking soda in a bowl; set aside. Beat butter, brown sugar, pudding mix, and white sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Beat in eggs, one at a time, until thoroughly blended, beating in vanilla extract with second egg. Add flour mixture; beat until just incorporated. Fold in white chocolate chips and cranberries until evenly distributed.
Drop spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto the prepared baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges become golden brown, 9 to 12 minutes. Cool on baking sheets for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Linda's Cranberry Cookies
raw_recipe.description: LInda's cranberry cookie recipe is packed with creamy white chocolate chips. The cookies are a delightful balance between soft, crunchy, sweet, and tart.

review.reviewBody: Best cookie ever! I subtituted rolled oats for the flour and made them oatmeal cranberry cookies instead though. So yummy!

These are great. I have never seen a 6 oz package of chocolate chips! I used 6 oz of semi-sweet chocolate chips, 6 oz white chocolate chips, 1/4 cup chopped walnuts, and the cranberries. I also added 1/4 tsp salt.

I used a stand mixer for everything, including the folding, because the dough is so stiff that it was impossible for me to work with otherwise. I used the "stir" setting.

I used a 1 T cookie scoop, but I didn't like it. The cookies weren't cooked all the way, and looked too much like chocolate chip cookies. I then cut each scoop in half, rolled each one into a ball, then flattened each ball. They can be very close together, as they spread very little. I was able to easily fit 20 half-tablespoon balls (then flattened) onto a 14x16 inch cookie sheet. I saw another similar recipe where they dipped half of each cookie in semi-sweet chocolate. They would definitely look fancier that way!

I flipflopped the white sugar/brown sugar amounts and used instant CHEESECAKE pudding. I also used four ounces dried cranberries, a little less than the amount of white chocolate chips I put in. The flavor of these cookies was amazing but they didn't want to spread much, I think maybe it was because I made the cookies too small. Next time, I'll make them bigger and see if they don't spread out a little better.
These cookies are the best! I make them all the time, exactly as the recipe is written. Sometimes I double or triple the recipe, bake some for now and freeze some dough to bake at a future date.
Turned out nice. I added about 1 Tbls of cornstarch to keep from flattening out so much. I will make again!

These cookies received rave reviews from everyone who tried them and were gone almost instantly! I followed the recipe almost exactly (I added more chocolate chips and cranberries than the recipe called for and rolled the dough by hand into 1 - 1.5 inch balls rather than dropping them by spoonfuls). The cookies were very easy to make. Highly recommended!

OMG, best cookies ever. Made them for Christmas to share with my family and I followed recipe to the letter except I mixed in 1 cup dried cranberries. These were so good and my sister in law can’t stop raving about them now she wants me to make them again. This recipe is definitely a keeper.

This is one of my favorite cookie recipes. At times I haven't been able to buy white chocolate chips and have used white Lindt Lindor bars chopped up. Sometimes I've added a few pecans into the mix. I can't make these very often, because I'd end up way fatter than I am.

Followed recipe to a T. One change that I would make to the original recipe would be to double the amount of white chocolate chips. Another change I would make would be to add a textural element such as coconut flakes or macadamia nuts. Overall, great recipe.....Cookie Monster approved :)

Great recipe, I omitted the white chips
and added the zest of one orange.
I have made this cookie many times
and I get many compliments.
These were delicious! After reading the other comments I did add about 1/4 teaspoon of salt and doubled (or maybe a little more) of the cranberries. Next time I may even add more cranberries.
Made as directed. Honestly, I'd omit the pudding next time, or try to find a sub. Adds an artificial flavor, but it DOES give a good texture.
Perfect cookies for any occasion!
My family loves these! We've tried several combinations. Chocolate pudding + peanutbutter chips is a favorite

I've made the recipe without the icing twice now and while the flavors are great, they still seem a little sweet. I do like adding almond extract and extra orange juice, but next time I won't add the white chocolate chips and I'll add some Oatmeal like I did on my first batch.
Really good. Well received by everyone - kids and grownups alike. I will make these again for sure. Thanks Linda!
Delish and easy
Great cookies , I love it
Great cookie. Having made the, I would cut the amount of white chocolate chips and add more cranberry, just to cut the sweetness, but overall, its really is a great cookie.
Best Christmas cookie that I made this year!
